object_context: Source-native higher-order semi-filter closure state induced by a selected family Λ of preservation pairs. Start from the generator traces required by 'above w', close upward, and repeatedly add E∩H (and its upward closure) whenever a registered pair (E,H) has both endpoints present. Determine whether this noncanonical closure state admits a fusion-aligned potential with a proved bounded per-new-pair increment while retaining enough structure to escape the C009/C025 canonical O(log N) ceiling.
qoi: A source-bound representation and accounting coordinate that (i) distinguishes unrestricted semi-filter preservation from canonical generator separation, (ii) changes by a provably bounded amount per added legal preservation pair, and (iii) is not already capped at O(log N) by canonical compression.

framework_binding.rakl_method_version: CANNOT_MEASURE: no RAKL_VERSION.json on current main

structural_coordinates: semi-filter state is upward closed, nonempty, and excludes the empty set
a semi-filter preserves (E,H) exactly when E,H in F implies E∩H in F
cover complexity asks for a minimum family Λ of preservation pairs for which no semi-filter above a target witness preserves all of Λ
the source proof of the cover/intersection-complexity relation builds a minimal closure by repeatedly adding pair intersections and upward closure until a fixed point
C024 shows one-pair fractional budgets can lose global correlation/integrality
C025 restores common-family correlation on G_NEQ but collapses to canonical/original-generator signatures with exact logarithmic capacity
the new state must therefore depend on recursively generated noncanonical intersections/closure membership, not only original generator labels
any lower-bound potential must control the marginal effect of one new fusion/preservation pair even in the presence of previously registered pairs

upward closure and reactivation of old pairs create a potential cascade/amplification channel that must be audited before using raw closure size, derivation depth, entropy, or number of newly derived intersections
equivalent_formulations: least fixed point of a monotone closure operator C_Λ on P(P(U)) generated by upward closure plus Horn-style rules E∧H => E∩H
forward-chaining state of a finite implicational system whose rules are indexed by selected fusion pairs
hypergraph reachability/closure state where pair endpoints jointly activate an intersection node
noncanonical semi-filter state tensor recording which arbitrary subsets become forced after recursive pair propagation
source-native alternative to generic lift-and-project variables: retain exactly the closure semantics already present in the cover-complexity proof

solved_or_near_solved_contexts.method: construct the least upward-closed family above a witness and propagate E∩H for every preserved pair until no new set appears
solved_or_near_solved_contexts.why_it_works: the resulting fixed point is the minimal candidate semi-filter satisfying the registered preservation rules; reaching ∅ witnesses impossibility of a preserving semi-filter
solved_or_near_solved_contexts.transfer_boundary: this gives an exact state representation but does not supply a bounded per-pair lower-bound potential

solved_or_near_solved_contexts.method: normalize source-justified canonical pairs to cuts and encode diagonal witnesses by common binary signatures
solved_or_near_solved_contexts.why_it_works: canonical unequal-pair coverage becomes signature injectivity and gives exact log2 N calibration
solved_or_near_solved_contexts.transfer_boundary: the state contains only original-generator separation and therefore cannot certify noncanonical full semi-filter structure

solved_or_near_solved_contexts.method: new facts activate pre-existing rules whose conclusions may recursively activate further rules
solved_or_near_solved_contexts.why_it_works: monotonicity yields a least fixed point independent of rule firing order
solved_or_near_solved_contexts.transfer_boundary: algorithmic closure depth/size can have large one-rule sensitivity and is not automatically a fusion lower-bound measure

method_transfer_matrix.source_context: Cavalar-Oliveira 2025 Definitions 18-21 and the closure construction in the proof machinery around Theorem 24
method_transfer_matrix.source_method: least fixed-point closure under upward closure and preservation-pair intersections
shared_structure: same semi-filter object and same legal preservation-pair semantics as the target cover problem
arbitrary subset/intersection state rather than only original generators
one selected pair is one fusion-aligned rule
enabling_assumptions: fixed target witness and its required generator traces
pair endpoints and intersections are subsets of U
disanalogies: the source closure proves feasibility/non-feasibility, not a quantitative super-log lower bound
one newly added pair may activate many previously dormant pairs, so naive state-growth accounting need not be locally bounded
method_transfer_matrix.repair_question: Can one quotient, charge, or rank closure events so a new pair has O(1) certified marginal charge despite arbitrary cascades, without collapsing back to canonical state?

method_transfer_matrix.source_method: dual weighting with unit mass per pair neighborhood
disanalogies: fractional weights erase integral multi-pair correlation
closure state is discrete and history-sensitive rather than an independent marginal weighting
method_transfer_matrix.repair_question: Can a closure-aware charge retain correlations while inheriting a certifiable per-pair budget?

cross_domain_analogy_scan.source_situation: one newly satisfied prerequisite can activate a long chain of already-present rules or dependent jobs
common_abstraction: latent rules become enabled when all antecedents are present
one local change can trigger a long global cascade
source_to_target_mapping: fact/job completion -> subset becomes forced in the semi-filter closure
dependency cascade -> recursive activation of older preservation pairs
shared_constraints: old rules persist and may fire only after a new derived state appears
disanalogies: software/build dependency length has no circuit-lower-bound authority
semi-filter upward closure additionally inserts all supersets
cross_domain_analogy_scan.proposed_transferable_principle: Before treating closure volume/depth as a lower-bound potential, test one-new-rule cascade sensitivity on source-native closure systems.
cross_domain_analogy_scan.falsifiable_validation_obligation: Construct or rule out a finite source-compatible closure system where adding one preservation pair forces an arbitrarily long chain of intersections through previously registered pairs.

explicit_disanalogies: noncanonical closure state is not automatically a strong lower-bound invariant
least-fixed-point exactness does not imply O(1)-Lipschitz sensitivity to one added pair
generic Horn-closure cascades need not be realizable by row/column generator traces of an explicit hard graph
a generic discrete-space hostile example can refute a universal accounting claim but cannot refute a graph-specific potential
large closure cardinality can reflect upward-closure combinatorics rather than root-critical cover complexity
derivation depth may depend on rule ordering unless defined via least parallel rounds; even then it may have high one-pair sensitivity
hostile_controls_required_before_candida: one-new-pair cascade through arbitrarily many previously dormant pairs
upward-closure amplification after deriving a small intersection
a target where closure representation is large but cover complexity is small
